newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch to launch first high-tech share index.
newsitem.headline: Dutch to launch first high-tech share index.

text.p: Dutch broker Wesselius and the national Central Bureau of Statistics (CBS) said on Friday they plan to start an index of high-tech stocks in the Netherlands.
"(Pending CBS approval) the CBS/Wesselius index for IT (information technology) funds will be in effect from the first of January 1997," Wesselius said in a statement.

"We're also planning to launch an investment vehicle on the same day. We're preparing a warrant on this IT index and aim for an options exchange listing on the day of the index's introduction," managing director Sem van Berkel told Reuters.
CBS is currently testing the weighting of the index which will include 17 stocks.

These funds include electronics giant Philips, Dutch PTT, printer and copier maker Oce van der Grinten, software maker CMG, information services provider Getronics, PC manufacturer Tulip, wafer stepper producer ASM Lithography and other chips, software and services companies.
"The index should give an accurate picture of the industry. One small move in Dutch PTT should not turn the entire index upside down," said specialist Cor Wijtvliet at Wesselius.
The Dutch high-tech sector is relatively young and lacks a large enough profile to attract investors.
But the rapid growth of these firms and their market capitalisation, totalling 13 percent of the Amsterdam Stock Exchange, underlines the necessity to improve understanding, Wesselius said.
"We need the approval stamp of the Statistics Bureau to give us the much needed credibility," Wijtvliet said.

Several Dutch high-tech companies have floated on New York's Nasdaq stock exchange and London's Alternative Investment Market in recent years, as they feared Amsterdam would not give them the same valuation or investment interest.
